blocks.en: Each role in the protocol is played by a separate agent that works from a written instruction. The lists below are abridged translations of these instructions.
blocks.zh: 协议中的每个角色都由一个单独的代理来扮演,从书面指令中发挥作用. 以下清单是这些说明的简略译本。

blocks.en: Instruction to the brainstorming agent (abridged, translated from the original)
blocks.zh: 向集思广益机构提供指导(简略,原文翻译)

blocks.en: 1. Start from a real scene, such as a work station, a home, a street, a sport, a game or a document. Do not look for a scene to dress up a mechanism you already like. 2. Inside the scene, find a hard constraint that a person who does this work would notice at a glance if it were drawn wrong. Only then ask whether it is difficult. 3. Say in one sentence who would need this picture and what they would do with it. This field is required. 4. Ask whether this picture existed in the world before we set the task. If not, the mechanism may still be good, but the carrier is a teaching prop: attach a real-life carrier and change nothing else. 5. A task must satisfy four things at once: it is a real commission; a layman can tell right from wrong in one look; the answer appears nowhere in the prompt; and judging it leaves behind a picture worth showing. 6. Tell your candidate in one sentence: what the viewer sees, where the mistake shows, and why this picture really exists. If you cannot, drop it. 7. Take the difficulty from what actually breaks models: withhold the key number; make a quantity travel from one place of the picture to another; make each cell depend on other cells; ask for a composite transform to be inverted; leave one step outside the rule table; give no scale at all. 8. Avoid what never breaks models: writing out the whole rule table for the model to follow; describing the final appearance; asking whether something appears anywhere in the image; exact counting on a regular layout. 9. Difficulty must come from the process, not the dose. More objects, more rows, more decimal places and more arithmetic are a ladder, not a new task. 10. To make a task harder, use a richer real specification or a real convention of the trade, or move the check to after the thing has been assembled. The amount of data stays the same. 11. One conversion, one addition or one comparison is allowed on any axis. Multi-step arithmetic belongs to the latent computation axis and may not be disguised. 12. Test the candidate three times. Hand the withheld number to the model for free: if the task becomes easy, it tests arithmetic. Reduce the count to five: if it becomes easy, it tests counting. Make the unusual rule normal again: if it is still hard, the difficulty is not where you said it was. 13. One task per mechanism. Two candidates are the same task if their failure conditions are the same sentence, whatever the objects are. Check for collisions across all nine capability axes, not only your own. 14. Do not clone the worked examples. Learn the formula, not the picture. 15. Before a candidate is released, name the nearest task that has already been scored, give its score, and say which specific quantity this candidate keeps outside the prompt. ‘It is harder’ is not an answer. 16. Declare anything you truncated, sampled or relaxed. You do not approve your own candidate: a reviewer does.

blocks.en: 1. Write the failure condition and the evaluation program before you write the prompt. 2. The prompt is a work order, not a construction drawing. It has four parts: the scene and the deliverable; the material that fixes the inputs; the purpose; and the constraints, including what must not appear. Never teach the model how to draw, and never state the answer. 3. Fix the input, not the output. Whatever the model should have before it starts may be given exactly. Whatever it should only produce after working may not appear. 4. List every element of the expected answer and confirm that at least one cannot be found word for word in the prompt. 5. A full rule table may be given, but after the table there must still be one step of computation, placement or conservation that cannot be looked up in it. 6. Do not lay the picture out element by element with a string of imperatives. That turns the model into a typesetter and measures nothing. Do not write down the final appearance. 7. The expected answer must promise something, and it must contain numbers. 8. A real industrial setting is not enough by itself. Its value is the part of the real specification that cannot fit in the prompt. Say which part that is. 9. For a task about orientation or visibility, fix the orientation with a natural anchor in the scene, such as a person reading the face of the object. Never state the camera-side conclusion, and never stay silent about orientation. 10. Rotate your own reference image by thirty degrees and score it again. If the score flips, the orientation was not fixed hard enough. State the sign convention wherever one shape could be read as two different signs. 11. If the VLM could answer the question from its own knowledge without looking at the image, the candidate is rejected. No rewording rescues it. 12. Answer two questions in writing. How could a model that knows nothing guess a score? How could a strong model get around the ability itself? Close both routes. 13. Require a result that cannot be faked by drawing, such as specific numbers or a correctly placed object. Do not ask whether something appears anywhere in the image. 14. No exact counting on a structured layout such as a table or a calendar. Counting tasks must scatter their objects. 15. Across the difficulty levels of one task, change at least two of carrier, setting, composition and style. Changing only the numbers is not enough. Re-skinning counts only if it changes the mechanism: counting apples and counting pears is one task, not two. 16. The picture that the prompt describes must have existed in the world before the task was set.

blocks.zh: 对评价方案代理机构的指示(简略,原文翻译)

blocks.en: 1. Perception belongs to the VLM and arithmetic belongs to code. The VLM never does arithmetic. Where the answer needs a computation, the VLM only reports what it sees in a machine-readable form, and a program computes the conclusion. 2. Every step must leave an overlay on the image that marks the element this step looked at. 3. Ask the VLM one observable fact at a time. Every ‘and’ belongs in code. Split a compound question into separate questions and combine them in code. 4. Every question must be answerable in seconds by a person with no background who is shown the crop. Move all domain knowledge into code. Only two kinds of question may need expertise: transcribing a notation, and marking geometry. 5. One question, one fact. No comparisons that are hard to follow, no double negatives, and no examples, because an example becomes the VLM’s target list. Fix the answer format. 6. Keep the phrase that names what to locate short. A long phrase breaks the check itself, and the symptom is a refusal to read, not a wrong number. 7. A question may never contain a correctness word, state an expectation, or reveal the shape of the expected answer. Never give the expected count to the step that proposes the boxes. The count is the answer. 8. Do not add a scene-level easy question by default. Only a real precondition earns one, because a scene check tends to reject the most correctly drawn images of an unusual task. 9. If the expected answer fixes the geometry, draw it over the image and ask whether it coincides. If the criterion is a geometric relation, draw the construction so that the conclusion is visible on the image. 10. A count that decides the score must go through the loop: locate, confirm, read, compute. The scored count is the number of items confirmed one by one, never the number of boxes proposed. Counts of at most ten are exempt. 11. Use only the allowed operators. A new operator needs a task-neutral design and at least three tasks that will reuse it. 12. Complexity is a defect. A task that no allowed operator can evaluate is better removed than kept. 13. There are three outcomes, never two: a scored result; a zero caused by the model’s own broken image; and a failure of the evaluator. A failure of the evaluator, or a refusal by the VLM, withholds the task and is never scored as zero. 14. Every zero must name the fact that was violated. That fact must be drawn on the image, and it must have been stated in plain words in the prompt. 15. Never change a threshold because of a score you have seen. The only valid reasons are the measured noise of the evaluator, consistency with similar tasks, and the arithmetic of the task itself.

VLM从不算术. 在答案需要计算的地方,VLM只报告它以机器可读形式看到的,一个程序计算结论. 2. 每一步骤都必须在标有这一步骤所看到要素的图像上留下一个叠加。 3. 一次询问一个可观察到的事实。 每一个“和”都属于代码。 将一个复合问题分成不同的问题,并把它们合并到代码中. 4. 每一个问题都必须由没有背景的人在几秒钟内回答,此人将展示作物。 将所有域知识移动到代码中 。 只有两种问题可能需要专门知识:转录标记和标记几何。 5. 一个问题,一个事实。 没有难以遵循的比较,没有双重负数,也没有例子,因为一个例子成为了VLM的目标列表. 修正答案格式。 6. 保留所要查找的简称。 一个长的短语打破了检查本身,症状是拒绝阅读,而不是错误的数字. 7. 问题可能永远不会包含正确的词、说明期望或揭示预期答案的形状。 千万不要把预期的数数给提出盒子的一步. 数是答. 8. 不默认添加场景级简易问题。 只有真实的前提条件才能赢得一个,因为场景检查往往会拒绝异常任务最正确绘制的图像. 9. 如果预期的答案修补几何,请将其画在图像上,并询问是否吻合。 如果标准是几何关系,则绘制构造,使结论在图像上可见. 10. 确定得分的计数必须经过循环:定位、确认、阅读、计算。 得分计数是逐项确认的项目数,决不是提议的箱数. 最多十点的计数可以豁免。 11. 只使用允许操作者。 新的操作员需要一种任务中性的设计,并且至少需要三项任务来重复使用. 12. 复杂性是一个缺陷。 不允许操作员评估的任务被删除比保存更好 。 13. 有三个结果,从来不是两个:得分结果;模型本身的破损图像造成的零;评价员的失败。 评价员的失败,或VLM拒绝,就扣留了任务,从未得分为零. 14. 每个零点必须说明被侵犯的事实。 这一事实必须照搬形象,并且必须立即用直白的文字加以说明。 15. 永远不要因为你看到的分数而改变门槛。 唯一有效的理由是评价者测得的噪音,与类似任务的一致性,以及任务本身的算术.

blocks.zh: 一次问VLM一个可观察到的事实. 每个“和”都属于代码。 将一个复合问题分成不同的问题,并把它们合并到代码中.

blocks.en: Every question must be answerable in seconds by a person with no background who is shown the crop. Move all domain knowledge into code. Only two kinds of question may need expertise: transcribing a notation, and marking geometry.
blocks.zh: 每个问题都必须由一个没有背景的人在数秒内回答,此人被显示作物. 将所有域知识移动到代码中 。 只有两种问题可能需要专门知识:转录标记和标记几何。

blocks.en: One question, one fact. No comparisons that are hard to follow, no double negatives, and no examples, because an example becomes the VLM’s target list. Fix the answer format.
blocks.zh: 一个问题,一个事实。 没有难以遵循的比较,没有双重负数,也没有例子,因为一个例子成为了VLM的目标列表. 修正答案格式。

blocks.en: You have a web search tool. Use it whenever the description depends on a fact you would otherwise be guessing at: a live or dated figure, the real appearance, markings, proportions or specification of an actual object, place, instrument or document. Search first, then draw what you found.
blocks.zh: 您有一个网络搜索工具 。 当描述取决于你所猜测的事实时使用它:活体或日期图、实际物体、地点、仪器或文件的真实外观、标记、比例或规格。 先搜索,然后画你找到的东西。

blocks.en: Search is yours to judge. A picture that needs no outside fact needs no search.
blocks.zh: 搜索是你的判断。 一个不需要外界事实的照片不需要搜索.

blocks.en: What you bring back from a search must end up in the code you write. The rendered page itself has no network: it cannot load a photograph, a font, a map tile or a data file from anywhere, so a fact is only useful once you have turned it into drawing instructions. Pasting a picture from the web would be collecting, not drawing, and the page cannot do it anyway.
blocks.zh: 你从搜索中带回来的 一定是你写的代码 渲染的页面本身没有网络:它不能从任何地方装入照片,字体,地图砖或数据文件,所以一个事实只有在你把它变成绘图指令时才有用. 从网络上粘贴一张图片是收集的,而不是绘制的,而且页面无论如何都无法完成.

blocks.en: The drawing surface is exactly {W} pixels wide and {H} pixels high. Fill it. Do not leave a border of blank page around the picture and do not draw outside it.
blocks.zh: 绘图表面是 {W} 像素宽和{H} 像素高。 灌顶. 不要在图片周围留下空白页的边框,不要在图片外画。

blocks.en: Use either a <canvas> element of exactly {W}x{H} with an inline <script> that draws on its 2D context, or one inline <svg> element of exactly {W}x{H}. Either is fine. Mixing them is fine.
blocks.zh: 使用精确 {W} x{H} 的 < canvas > 元素, 并带有内含的 <script > , 并借鉴其 2D 上下文, 或 精确 {W} x{H} 的一个内含的 < svg> 元素。 都无所谓 混合他们很好。

blocks.en: Give the page a background. A transparent or default-white page counts as an undrawn picture.
blocks.zh: 给页面一个背景. 透明或默认的白页计为未刷新图片 。

blocks.en: Everything is inline in the one document. No , no , no external
blocks.zh: 所有事情都包含在一个文件中。 没有,没有,没有外部

blocks.en: Text must use fonts already on a normal machine. Name generic families such as sans-serif, serif, monospace, or common system faces with a generic fallback.
blocks.zh: 文本必须在普通机器上已经使用字体 。 命名通用家族,如sans-serif,serif,单空间,或带有通用回落的共同制度面孔.

blocks.en: No alert, confirm or prompt. No window.open. No timers that keep changing the picture: draw the finished picture, do not animate it.
blocks.zh: 没有警报,确认或迅速。 没有窗户,打开 没有计时器持续更改图片:绘制完成的图片,不要动画.

blocks.en: Draw on load, synchronously if you can.
blocks.zh: 提取负载,如果可以同步进行.

blocks.en: The moment the drawing is complete, set window.__done = true. A screenshot is taken as soon as that flag appears, so setting it early gives you a half-drawn picture and never setting it costs you nothing but a wait.
blocks.zh: 画完成时, 设置窗口。 。 一旦旗帜出现,就会拍下截图, 所以提早设定它会给你一个半拖拉拉的照片, 从不设定它只需要等待。

blocks.en: The document must not throw. An uncaught exception is a blank page and scores nothing.
blocks.zh: 文件不能丢出。 一个未发现的例外是空白的一页,没有得分.

blocks.en: Draw everything the description asks for, with the counts, the positions, the text, the relations and the values it names. Every quantity in the description is checkable in the picture afterwards, so compute it in code rather than eyeballing it: lay out with arithmetic, place things by coordinates you work out, and write the labels the description dictates, spelled exactly as it spells them.
blocks.zh: 绘制描述所要求的一切,与计数,位置,文本,关系以及它命名的值一起. 描述中的每个数量都可以在照片中检查, 所以用代码来计算,而不是看它: 用算术来计算,通过坐标来排列事物, 并写下描述要求的标签, 拼写得准确。

blocks.en: You get one attempt and you never see the rendered result, so prefer constructions you can be sure of over constructions that need tuning by eye.
blocks.zh: 你得到一个尝试,你从来没有看到 得到的结果, 所以更喜欢的建筑 你可以确定 而不是建筑需要通过眼睛调整。

blocks.en: Make it look like the thing described, not like a diagram of the thing, unless a diagram is what was described.
blocks.zh: 让它看起来像描述的东西, 而不是一个事物的图, 除非一个图表是描述。

blocks.en: Reply with exactly one fenced code block, opened with three backticks and the word html, and nothing before or after it. No explanation, no notes, no second block.
blocks.zh: 以一个有栅栏的代码块进行回复,打开时有三个回击和html字,前后无一字. 没有解释,没有笔记,没有第二个街区。
